newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek curve flat, 3-,5-yr bonds up, ecu/drs idles.
newsitem.headline: Greek curve flat, 3-,5-yr bonds up, ecu/drs idles.

text.p: Greek depos and forex forwards were stuck in tight ranges, three- and five-year bonds were well bid and ecu/drachma was hovering around 309.90, unaffected by a rise in June inflation to 5.5 percent from 5.4 percent in May, dealers said.
"Depos and forex forwards are holding Thursday afternoon levels," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "The market had discounted a pick up in inflation leaving the interbank curve intact."
The National Statistics Service said CPI-based inflation rose to 5.5 percent year-on-year in June from 5.4 percent in May.
Some traders said they expected rates to rise due to a shortage in overnight liquidity later on but others predicted that rates would ease on improved liquidity.
Bond traders said prices of three-year bonds due 2000 were trading 30 basis points higher to 99.50/85 and five-year bonds due 2002 were up 20 to 25 basis points to 98.25/50.
"Trading in seven-and 10-year bonds is thin today and their prices little changed," said a bond dealer at a private bank.
The mark was quoted at 157.43/53 from Thursday's 157.705 fix, the dollar at 275.45/55 drachmas from 276.380 and the ecu at 309.83/93 from 309.99 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma is hovering around 309.80/95 in calm trading," said a forex dealer. "U.S. markets are closed today and forex markets are quiet today."
